title: Largest Local Values in a Matrix
statement: Return an (n-2) by (n-2) matrix where each cell is the maximum value in the corresponding 3-by-3 window of the input grid.
explanation: For each center cell that is not on the border, scan its surrounding 3-by-3 window and store the maximum.

title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
approach: Minimum white blocks in a length-k window
statement: Return the minimum number of white blocks that must be recolored so some substring of length k contains only black blocks.
explanation: Slide a window of length k while tracking black blocks; minimize k minus the black count.

title: Minimum Hours of Training to Win a Competition
approach: Train energy and experience before opponents
statement: Return the minimum training hours needed so initial energy and experience exceed each opponent's corresponding values when encountered.
explanation: Energy training must make initial energy greater than total opponent energy; experience is increased just enough before any opponent whose experience is not lower.

title: Removing Stars From a String
approach: Use a stack to remove prior characters
statement: Process the string where each '*' removes the closest preceding non-star character, and return the remaining string.
explanation: Push ordinary characters; on a star, pop the most recent character.

title: Find Subarrays With Equal Sum
statement: Return true if two different length-two subarrays have the same sum.
explanation: Compute every adjacent pair sum and return true when a sum is encountered for the second time.

title: Most Frequent Even Element
approach: Count even values and break ties by smaller value
statement: Return the even number with the highest frequency, choosing the smallest number when frequencies tie; return -1 if there is no even number.
explanation: Count only even values, then select by frequency descending and numeric value ascending.

title: Smallest Even Multiple
statement: Return the smallest positive integer that is divisible by both n and 2.
explanation: If n is already even, it is the answer; otherwise twice n is the smallest even multiple.

title: Sort the People
statement: Return the names sorted from tallest to shortest.
explanation: Pair each name with its height and order pairs by height descending.

title: Number of Common Factors
statement: Return the number of positive integers that divide both a and b.
explanation: Check each integer from 1 through min(a,b) and count those dividing both values.

title: The Employee That Worked on the Longest Task
approach: Compare task durations from end timestamps
statement: Given employees' task end times in chronological order, return the employee ID with the longest single task; choose the smallest ID on a tie.
explanation: The first task duration equals its end time; later durations are the difference between consecutive end times. Track the longest duration and resolve ties by smaller ID.
